reviews.title: Steals passwords and private information and overuses generative AI
reviews.text:
Facemoji does NOT disclose or share many policies about privacy and demands full access of what you type without actual reasoning or an explanation. If you pay attention and look closely at its requirements on the Settings app, you'll immediately see that it doesn't say that allowing full access to everything you type makes Facemoji ABLE to add its keyboards, rather that you have to do it or they won't add the keyboards. It seems like they could add the keyboard feature either way, but they specifically want you to give them full access to every letter you type whilst using their app, which is why you need to click the "Allow Full Access" option to unlock more features on Facemoji. I've also researched the app, and its lack of disclosure on the privacy it provides (or should I say, lack of) is concerning.
It also uses generative AI for tasks and messages that are frankly quite stupid and useless. No, Facemoji, I actually don't want to waste gallons of drinkable water and take homes away from innocent animals and children to find out how to send my messages in Kim Kardashian's style or generate outdated AI slop "comebacks" always ending in "😏".
In conclusion, I regret downloading Facemoji and do not recommend it at all. It exploits children and their privacy, and it's full of low-quality, terrible generative AI features.

reviews.title: Wonderful app, but it includes closed symbols and not many free fonts.
reviews.text:
I love the design of the app overall and custom keyboards! Sadly a lot of the fonts you need to pay for, and in the past I've been able to use fonts that have suddenly changed to payment required, and some of the pay to use fonts aren't even that unique. Another major issue is that closed symbols (symbols that are part of cultures that people shouldn't be using unless they're used in said culture) is included without warning in the keyboard--meaning those who use the app could offend others without intention, and overall they just shouldn't be used.
Please remove these symbols or at least add a warning to them if possible so people don't use them accidentally!

reviews.title: Keylogger
reviews.text:
I went from never having a hacked account in my life to repeated suspicious login attempts within a week of downloading Facemoji. I have done nothing different besides having this app. Order of elimination only has one change in the change pool. ETA: the developer reply doesn’t address the fact I DL from app store and the suspicious login attempts stopped immediately after deleting the app. If it’s not supposed to have security concerns like this Facemoji needs to look into why this happened.
Edit2: responding to dev:  I started getting attempted suspicious logins from facebook. Most of them were coming from taiwan where a lot of phishing scams are run out of. I did some searching on the origins and I’m not the only one who has gotten suspicious login attempts from there. But the only thing I had done differently was this app and it stopped after I deleted the app. If the app was trying to log into my facebook without asking that would be bad enough but for the ip address to be almost 8000 miles away from me, that is a different problem. 
Edit3: I originally thought it was the app trying to connect, but that wouldn’t explain the IP address coming from another country. The only thing I could come up that made sense is someone is using your app to grab passwords. Unless the login attempt reroutes thru an internal server; so it’s login on from your country. But that’s a fairly alarming way to connect.
